title: Pilot Outage / No Pilot
shortDescription: Gas valve does not detect pilot flame.
fullDescription:
On State gas water heaters, a single LED flash on the gas control valve indicates pilot outage — the thermopile is not generating enough millivolts to keep the pilot valve open.

Most commonly the thermopile has weakened with age, or the pilot orifice is clogged with dust or spider webs (FVIR units especially).
safetyWarning: If you smell gas, do not light. Ventilate and call gas utility.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Check manual gas valve open and other appliances work.

fixSteps.title: Test thermopile
fixSteps.instruction: Measure millivolts at gas valve TH-TP terminals; should be 600-800mV.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermopile
fixSteps.instruction: Install matching OEM thermopile.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if pilot will not stay lit after thermopile swap.

title: Pilot Will Not Light / Gas Valve Fault
shortDescription: Pilot ignition attempted but no flame detected.
fullDescription: Two flashes mean the pilot did not light during the ignition attempt. Causes include no gas, blocked orifice, or failed igniter on power-vent models.

fixSteps.title: Purge gas line
fixSteps.instruction: If recently shut off, hold pilot button longer to bleed air.

fixSteps.title: Clean pilot assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum FVIR air intake screen and pilot tube.

whenToCallPro: If pilot still will not light.

title: Thermopile / Thermocouple Voltage Low
fullDescription: Three flashes warn the thermopile millivolt output is below the gas valve hold-in threshold. Pilot may light but burner may not stay on.

fixSteps.title: Tighten connections
fixSteps.instruction: TH-TP terminals at gas valve.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermopile
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM part.

whenToCallPro: If new thermopile does not help.

title: Tank Temperature Exceeds Limit
fullDescription:
Four flashes indicate the tank temperature sensor read above the safety limit (typically 190F). Gas valve will lock out.

Possible causes: failed gas valve, scale buildup, or thermostat failure.
safetyWarning: Hot water can scald. Allow tank to cool before service.

fixSteps.title: Allow cooldown
fixSteps.instruction: Let tank cool 1 hour before reset.

fixSteps.title: Replace gas valve
fixSteps.instruction: OEM matched valve, requires gas leak test.

title: Sensor Failure
shortDescription: Tank temperature sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: Five flashes mean the tank temperature sensor input is invalid. On most State models the sensor is integrated with the gas valve.

fixSteps.title: Replace gas valve
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor usually integrated.

title: Combustion Air Blocked / FVIR Trip
shortDescription: Air intake screen blocked or vapor sensor tripped.
fullDescription: Six flashes on FVIR-equipped State water heaters indicate the combustion air screen is blocked with lint and dust, or the vapor sensor detected flammable vapors.
safetyWarning: Never store gasoline or solvents near a gas water heater.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum air screen
fixSteps.instruction: Use vacuum on bottom intake screen of tank.

fixSteps.title: Remove vapor sources
fixSteps.instruction: Move paint, gasoline, solvents away from heater.

title: Gas Valve Internal Failure
fullDescription: Seven flashes indicate the integrated gas control board has an internal failure. The valve must be replaced.
safetyWarning: Gas valve work requires leak testing.

fixSteps.title: Call pro
fixSteps.instruction: Replace gas valve.

faq.a: State often covers 6-10 years on parts.

title: Electric Element Open / Failed
fullDescription: On State electric tank water heaters with digital control, E1 indicates an open heating element. Tank scale and burnout from dry-firing are common causes.
safetyWarning: Turn off breaker before service. 240V can be lethal.
symptoms: No hot water (one element) or lukewarm only

fixSteps.title: Test elements
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; measure resistance — open circuit means failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace element
fixSteps.instruction: Drain tank, swap element, refill before powering up.

whenToCallPro: If unfamiliar with 240V wiring or draining tank.

title: ECO / High Limit Trip
shortDescription: Energy cutoff tripped due to overheat.
fullDescription: E2 indicates the ECO (Energy Cut Off) on the upper thermostat tripped because tank water exceeded ~170F. Usually caused by a stuck thermostat.
safetyWarning: Hot water hazard; allow tank to cool.

fixSteps.title: Press reset button
fixSteps.instruction: Red ECO reset on upper thermostat assembly.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: If trips repeatedly, swap upper thermostat.

title: No Ignition (Tankless)
fullDescription: Code 11 on State tankless gas water heaters means no ignition was detected. Causes include closed gas valve, low gas pressure, or air in line on initial install.
safetyWarning: Check for gas odor before retry.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm valve fully open and other appliances work.

fixSteps.title: Reset and retry
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle to retry ignition; allow line to bleed.

fixSteps.title: Check gas line size
fixSteps.instruction: Tankless needs 3/4 in. supply for most BTU ratings.

whenToCallPro: Call pro if gas pressure or line size issue.

faq.a: Larger gas line and dedicated venting.
